slides.title: Entering the US market
Key questions

claims.claim: Should Onsoo enter the US market in 2027, and if so, by which route, within $18M of peak cash and with payback by 2030?
evidence: Sub-questions: 1 Is the US a better use of the one 2027 launch than a Japan scale-up? 2 Does a national specialty-retail launch in 2027 meet the board's tests? 3 Does an Amazon-led launch meet the board's tests? 4 Does the Amazon case hold if ad costs, tariffs or sales growth go against plan? 5 How should Onsoo launch, and what would make it change course?
Decision maker: CEO and board of Onsoo Botanicals, choosing the 2027 new-market launch

Success criteria: A US business on the way to $40M of revenue by 2030; Peak negative cumulative US cash of no more than $18M through 2030; Cumulative US cash back to zero by the end of 2030; Group operating margin at or above 8% in every year; Only one major new-market launch in 2027
Timing: Board meeting, March 2027
Out of scope: Markets other than the US and Japan; Routes the planning team did not model (DTC-led, mass retail); Exchange-rate scenarios

slides.title: Four gates tell the board early whether to scale, fix or stop the US launch, led by the ad-cost ceiling

claims.claim: Ad cost (ACoS) gate — Most important gate
evidence: Track: Amazon ad spend as a share of Amazon sales, each quarter
Threshold: At or below 28.6%; 26.9% if duty rises to 25%
If missed: Cut spend on the weakest keywords and SKUs before adding budget
Each percentage point costs about $0.7M of cash by 2030

claims.claim: Sales pace gate — Stops a stall early
evidence: Track: Amazon units against plan, end-2027
Threshold: 300,000 units in 2027, and well above the 168,000 June 2026 pace
If missed: Cut fixed costs and pause new SKUs

claims.claim: Tariff gate — Resets the ceiling
evidence: Track: US duty on Korean cosmetics, decision in mid-2027
Threshold: 15% today; 25% possible
If missed: Re-run the case and lower the ACoS ceiling

claims.claim: Retail trigger gate — Opens retail
evidence: Track: Aided awareness among category buyers, and Amazon sales
Threshold: Above 20% awareness and above $10M of Amazon sales
If missed: Stay Amazon-led and retest a year later

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Enter the US in 2027 through Amazon, not national retail, and cap ad costs at 28.6% of sales so the launch pays back by 2030. The board is asked to approve three decisions at its March 2027 meeting: (1) Approve the Amazon-led US entry for 2027; (2) Hold the launch to four gates (ad cost ACoS ceiling, sales pace, tariff, retail trigger); (3) Restate the $40M ambition as a goal beyond 2030. Open retail only above 20% awareness, raising the CEO's retail trigger from 15%.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended: passes on plan; payback needs ACoS at or below 28.6%. Peak cash need $1.9M; 2030 US revenue $26.4M (66% of $40M ambition).

alternatives_considered.option: Option B · Retail-led (national specialty-retail launch, 600 doors)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Reject: breaks the cap and the floor even on its own plan. Peak cash need $20.8M; group margin 4.5% in 2027; sell-through at 4% awareness 2.6 units/door/week vs 4.0 cut-off; 1.3x Amazon halo rests on a correlation.
Safe, but builds no US business; adds $7.0M of revenue by 2030 and $1.8M of operating profit at low risk. Held back under the one-launch rule.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO's initial hypothesis (retail trigger at 15% awareness, ACoS falling to 25%, cross-border seller, $40M by 2030, duty fixed at 15%)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Plan keeps the CEO's Amazon-first idea but raises the retail trigger to 20%, sets a 28.6% ACoS ceiling, moves to own US entity, adds a stall case and end-2027 review, restates ambition to $26.4M by 2030 / $40M after retail, re-runs case after tariff decision.
Left out on purpose: not modeled by the planning team; DTC is 12% and mass retail 14% of K-beauty skincare sales.
Left out: no cost or door data for a small test; it returns at the 20% awareness trigger.
Left out: outside management's control and only an upside; the pack gives no FX path.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Payback hinges on ad cost: ACoS must stay at or below 28.6%; at the 32% benchmark, cumulative cash ends 2030 at −$2.3M; each percentage point of ACoS moves cumulative cash by $0.7M
Plan's 25% ACoS assumes ACoS falls as the brand matures, but costs per click rise as brands bid on broader keywords; agency median at this scale is 32% (range 26%–38%)
US tariff decision expected mid-2027; a rise from 15% to 25% duty cuts 35 cents per unit and lowers the ACoS ceiling to 26.9%; duty applied at 25% from 2027 as the harsher case
Sales could stall, as for two of three Amazon-first peers; stall case at the June 2026 pace would cost $6.8M by 2030 (our estimate, sales flat at 12 × the June 2026 pilot month)
The ACoS ceiling holds the plan's volumes and costs fixed
The planning team applies the hero product's per-unit economics to all SKUs
Only inventory counts as working capital: the pack gives no Amazon payout lag or receivables; one-time costs run through operating profit; inventory is not released in 2030
The briefing pack gives no working capital for Japan; Option J peak cash need is its 2027 operating loss
Amazon halo of 1.3x rests on a cross-brand correlation (0.71 across 30 brands); no cause shown
Repeat rate: unclear whether more SKUs raise it; track it from the first 2027 cohort
The four SKUs added in 2027 will need to match the 4.5-star rating
2027 plan of 300,000 units needs 1.8 times the June pilot pace, with seven SKUs instead of three
Out of scope: markets other than the US and Japan; routes not modeled (DTC-led, mass retail); exchange-rate scenarios
Five figures in the board material need correcting before the board relies on them ($5.2B market, 4.5 sell-through, 1.3x halo, 25% ACoS, 15% awareness trigger)
